headline: Grandmother of 12 Breaks Her Own Guinness World Record by Holding a Plank for Five Hours

sources.excerpt: A grandmother of 12 is being credited for breaking her own Guinness World Record for a woman holding a plank move for the longest time period. DonnaJean Wilde made her potential record-breaking attempt at the Huntsman World Senior Games in Utah this week and completed a plank hold for five hours. Guinness World Records confirmed to ABC News that Wilde's title record, which she achieved on March 21, 2024, is 4 hours, 30 minutes and 11 seconds. The organization said it has received an application for Wilde's newest record attempt and will review evidence before declaring a new record. "I always wondered if I could have gone to five [hours]," Wilde told ABC News' Danny New of her motivation to break her own plank hold record. According to World Senior Games, the record attempt began at 3:03 p.m. MT, with judges rotating out every hour until 8:03 p.m. MT, when Wilde's attempt ended. "Some of them would come right down to me: 'Go, DonnaJean, go! You're doing great!'" Wilde said of the judges. The 61-year-old, who lives in Alberta, Canada, said her training to prepare for her record attempt included having her 3-year-old granddaughter, Rose, lie on her back while she planked. Wilde said she wasn't certain she would be able to accomplish her five-hour feat and even considered giving up during the attempt. "I told [my husband] Randy, 'I'm done. I'm going down.' And they [the audience] all chanted me to the end. They got me through the last 10 minutes," Wilde said. If her latest record attempt is recognized, Wilde would have earned her third Guinness title, following her previous plank record and her other record for the most pushups done in an hour by a woman, at 1,575. It's another impressive feat for Wilde, who said she didn't rest for long after her latest plank feat. The morning after her record attempt, she ran in a 3,000-meter race. As for her next record attempt, Wilde said she hopes to do at least 1,600 pushups in an hour and break her second record title.

A 61-year-old Canadian grandmother broke the female abdominal plank world record after holding the position for five hours. DonnaJean Wilde accomplished the feat at the Huntsman World Senior Games in Utah on Oct. 4, breaking her own record by nearly 30 minutes, Storyful reported. Wilde’s plank began at 3:03 p.m. and ended at 8:03 p.m., with several judges rotating in and out of shifts during that period, a spokesperson for the World Senior Games told Storyful. Her previous record of 4 hours, 30 minutes and 11 seconds was set on March 21, 2004, at the Canadian high school where she once served as vice principal, according to the Guinness Book of World Records. "To successfully achieve the record, the challenger’s forearms and toes must touch the ground at all times," Guinness states. "The remainder of the body must be lifted off the ground and be kept straight throughout," it also says. "My elbows hurt pretty bad," Wilde said after completing the previous record. "I was so worried about losing my form, and I think that’s why my quads hurt because I was just really tense." She shared with Guinness that the first two hours "went by quickly," but the next two hours were much more difficult. "The last hour was the most challenging, just to stay focused and keep my form," she said. During the last 30 minutes, she said she focused on "breathing, staying calm and not shaking." Wilde first added planking to her daily routine years ago after breaking her wrist because she could perform the exercise while wearing a cast. "I realized that I could read and do things when I was planking and fell in love with it," she said, according to the report. Wilde shared some advice for others aiming to hold extended planks. "Keep trying and keep practicing. When you have to read or work on your computer, just get on the floor and do it on the floor." Wilde has 12 grandchildren, according to Guinness. Her new record is pending review and approval by Guinness.
